experiments.title: Experiment 1: Baseline Efficiency & Scaling (Ideal Channel)
experiments.description: Evaluates raw sifting efficiency, distillable key yield, and execution runtime scaling with qubit count under zero noise and zero eavesdropping.

experiments.title: Experiment 2: Channel Noise Robustness & Security Thresholds
experiments.description: Quantifies the degradation of QBER and Bell parameter |S| as depolarizing noise increases, pinpointing the exact abort threshold for each protocol.

experiments.title: Experiment 3: Intercept-Resend Attack Detection Sensitivity
experiments.description: Evaluates the sensitivity of each protocol to active quantum channel eavesdropping across interception intensities (0% to 100%).

experiments.title: Experiment 4: Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) Attack & Classical Channel Authentication
experiments.description: Demonstrates that quantum mechanics cannot prevent a MitM attack without pre-shared classical channel authentication (HMAC basis verification).

experiments.title: Experiment 5: Finite-Key Statistical Convergence & Stability
experiments.description: Examines statistical variance, false alarm rates, and estimation stability across sample sizes (small vs large pulse counts).

scorecard.Key Insight / Winner: BB84 produces double the raw sifted key per transmitted photon.
B92 is highly sensitive to noise; BB84 & E91 tolerate higher fiber losses.
E91 provides the strongest security: verifiable without trusting source.
E91 detects Eve even before calculating classical key errors.
B92 requires the simplest optical transmitter (only 2 laser diodes).
Quantum physics cannot prevent MitM alone; classical HMAC is mandatory.
